dedupe_keys.name: radio society of sri lanka vhf repeater network hf beacon and echolink gateway

description: The Radio Society of Sri Lanka describes the communications infrastructure it operates for licensed amateur radio operators, which also supports emergency communications when needed: a network of VHF repeaters, an HF beacon and digital gateways. For each repeater the page gives status, input and output frequencies, mode, access tone, location with coordinates, elevation, antenna and links. The backbone repeater on Pidurutalagala, the highest point of the island at 2,524 metres, sits at a Civil Aviation site; the Yatiyanthota repeater at an ITN transmitting station at 1,308 metres covers the Western Province and almost a third of the island; the two are linked on 438.600 MHz UHF to form one network used by a nightly VHF net. The Deniyaya repeater is down for repair and the Nuwara Eliya repeater has been decommissioned. RSSL also hosts the 4S7B beacon of the Northern California DX Foundation international HF beacon network and runs the Echolink node 4S7RS-R around the clock. Access is free and public; the site states all rights reserved. Caveats: the list covers only the society's own sites. Coverage is Sri Lanka. The site menu also links a 2025 cyclone emergency communications operation report. It supports emergency communications planning; related records are the WIA Australian repeater directory and the NRRL Norway repeater list.
